name: What is chinking, and why is it essential during log home refinishing?

mainEntity.name: What is chinking, and why is it essential during log home refinishing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Log chinking is a flexible textured sealant applied between log courses to seal gaps against air infiltration, water, insects, and heat loss. While traditional chinking was mortar-based and tended to crack with seasonal log shifting, modern chinking is made of high-performance elastomeric acrylic that stretches and compresses as timbers move. During refinishing, cracked or pulling-away chinking must be cut out and renewed with proper backing rod before sealing the wood. Maintaining intact chinking preserves interior energy efficiency and prevents water from pooling behind logs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Chinking is flexible synthetic sealant installed between log joints that moves with the timbers. It keeps out drafts, moisture, and pests while protecting against log rot.
